record.paper_title: Negative Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Given an unsigned graph Γ and a specified set B of circles of Γ, determine whether there exists a signature σ:E(Γ)→{+,−} such that the negative circles of the signed graph Σ=(Γ,σ) are exactly the circles in B.

evidence.quote: 1. Can a given set B of circles in Γ be the negative circles of a signature? Ans. Easy: B is a negative circle set iff every theta subgraph of Γ has, among its three circles, either one or three that belong to B [18].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Γ = (V, E) be a finite unsigned graph. A circle (cycle) of Γ is the edge set of a simple closed walk in Γ. A signature of Γ is a map σ : E → {+, −}; the pair Σ = (Γ, σ) is called a signed graph. The sign of a circle C in Σ is the product ∏_{e ∈ C} σ(e); C is called negative if this product equals −. A theta subgraph of Γ is a subgraph consisting of two distinct vertices joined by three internally disjoint paths; such a subgraph contains exactly three circles (the three pairwise unions of the paths).

Given Γ and a specified family B of circles of Γ, determine a necessary and sufficient combinatorial condition on B for the existence of a signature σ : E → {+, −} such that the set of negative circles of Σ = (Γ, σ) is exactly B. In particular, prove or disprove: such a signature σ exists if and only if, for every theta subgraph of Γ, the number of its three circles that belong to B is either 1 or 3.
artifact.status_search_result: The characterization is classical: a family B of circles is realizable as the set of negative circles of some signature on Γ if and only if every theta subgraph of Γ has either one or three of its three circles in B. This is attributed to Zaslavsky and is recorded as a known easy result in the problem collection on negative circles in signed graphs.

status_evidence.title: Negative Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
status_evidence.snippet: B is a negative circle set iff every theta subgraph of Γ has, among its three circles, either one or three that belong to B.
status_evidence.claim: The realizability question is solved by the theta-subgraph (1-or-3) condition.
